# ntfuzz dashboard API

> Read fuzzing projects, targets, run diagnostics, coverage, and crash stacks as JSON without running the browser terminal or JavaScript.

All URLs below are relative to this dashboard's origin. GET requests need no request body. This guide and OpenAPI description cover the read endpoints shared by serve and view.

## Investigate a crash

1. GET /api/status. Check read_only and snapshot_at. A snapshot is historical data, not live worker activity; updated_at also equals its publication time. Report snapshot_at when describing freshness. Live mode uses updated_at for response time.
2. GET /api/crashes?open=true (or GET /api/crashes/{id} for a single crash). Match project_name, package, and target_name (exact spelling). An empty array means no matching open crashes in this data, not proof that a target is bug-free.
3. Read stack, first_seen, last_seen, git_sha, dirty, go_version, input_hash, stack_fingerprint, issue_url, blamed_module, blamed_version, blamed_file, blamed_line, blamed_url, and replay_status. fixed_at is omitted for open crashes; issue_url on an open crash means it has been reported upstream.
4. Open GET /crashes/{id} for a server-rendered HTML permalink, or GET /api/crashes/{id}/report.md for a Markdown advisory report with reproduction instructions.
5. Download the Go fuzz corpus reproducer file from GET /api/crashes/{id}/input when public_inputs is true on the project (always available in serve mode; returns HTTP 403 in snapshot view mode when public_inputs is false). Place the file in testdata/fuzz/FuzzX/<input_hash> and run `go test ./<pkg> -run 'FuzzX/<input_hash>'`.
6. Use the crash's numeric target_id in GET /api/runs?target=8&limit=2 (replace 8 with the actual ID). Review status and diagnostic for recent execution evidence. A historical crash need not have occurred in the latest run.
7. For a target without an open crash, GET /api/targets?project=PROJECT_NAME and match name and package; use its id. URL-encode parameter values. Numeric IDs avoid ambiguity across packages/projects.

minimized_input records the server-local corpus file path; use GET /api/crashes/{id}/input to download the corpus bytes when the project opts in via `public_inputs: true` (or on a live serve instance). Newly recorded stacks scrub local checkout and GOMODCACHE prefixes to module paths.

## Read endpoints

- [Status](/api/status): fleet summary, read_only, and snapshot_at when applicable.
- [Projects](/api/projects): project IDs, names, revisions, public_inputs, and sync status.
- [Targets](/api/targets): active targets; optional project filter accepts project ID or name.
- [Open crashes](/api/crashes?open=true): defaults to open only; open=false or open=all includes fixed crashes. Optional target filter.
- Per-crash endpoints: `/api/crashes/{id}` (JSON), `/crashes/{id}` (server-rendered HTML permalink), `/api/crashes/{id}/report.md` (Markdown report), and `/api/crashes/{id}/input` (Go corpus file download).
- [Runs](/api/runs?limit=2): most recent first; optional target filter; limit defaults to 100.
- [Coverage history](/api/coverage/history?target=8&limit=50): replace example target ID; chronological series of the most recent points, default limit 50. Missing target returns an empty array.
- [Time-series stats](/api/stats/throughput?window=24h): canned time-bucketed queries (`throughput`, `coverage`, `outcomes`, `revisions`, `burndown`) over windows (`1h`, `6h`, `24h`, `7d`, `14d`) with optional `project` and `target` filters.

Target filters accept numeric ID, target name, or project-qualified target name (project/name). Prefer IDs. Positive integer limits are supported; missing or invalid limits use the default. List responses are JSON arrays; failures return an error string in a JSON object. open accepts true/1, false/0/all; invalid values return HTTP 400.

## Documentation

- [API documentation](/api/docs): browser-readable usage guide.
- [OpenAPI description](/openapi.json): schemas and parameters for the read API.

Public snapshot viewers expose no mutation endpoint. Private live servers also support POST /api/crashes/{id}/issue (to link an upstream issue URL to an open crash) and POST /api/crashes/{id}/fix; those operator mutations change stored state and are not needed to investigate a crash.

Revision/recovery tracking: GET /api/stats/revisions?window=24h; GET /api/crash-replays for saved-input checks. Baselines are not new commits; replay pass means the saved input no longer reproduces.

GET /api/stats/burndown returns open-crash backlog and new/reopened/resolved counts. history_estimated_before labels reconstructed older history. Graphs support per-terminal Kitty image rendering with the i key and text fallback.
